# The definition of "required for merge" for vizra-user (ADR-002, "CI fan-in
# and merge queue").
#
# scripts/ci/require-checks.sh reads this file in the `ci-required` job and
# fails unless every entry is satisfied for the commit under test. Exactly ONE
# required status check is configured on the branch ruleset — `ci-required` —
# and this file is the single place the required set is declared and reviewed.
#
# Syntax (one check-run name per line, as GitHub reports it — matrix legs carry
# their leg in the name):
#   name    must EXIST for this commit and must conclude `success`
#   ?name   required only IF it ran (path-filtered lanes)
#
# Nothing but `success` passes: `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `neutral` and
# `skipped` all fail (AGENTS.md: a skipped required lane is not a pass).
#
# This file is owner-reviewed (CODEOWNERS, once the ruleset is applied): a PR
# that weakens the required set must be as visible as one that weakens a test.

# frontend-ci.yml — the canonical `npm run ci` gate: lint (including the
# ADR-003 identity/caching rules), typecheck, vitest, production build.
frontend

# contract-ci.yml — the vendored vizra-core contract matches its manifest, and
# lib/api/generated.ts is byte-for-byte what the pinned generator produces from
# it. This is the check that makes "the client is generated, never hand-edited"
# (VZ-FOUND-002) true rather than aspirational. Never drop it to unblock a
# merge.
contract

# ci-guard.yml — action pins, no hidden continue-on-error, `npm ci` not
# `npm install`, required-checks.txt names only jobs that exist, scripts/ci is
# shellchecked, and the fan-in passes its own regression suite. Path-filtered
# to .github/** and scripts/ci/**, so it is optional-if-absent.
?guard

# docker-build.yml — the production Dockerfile builds on the acceptance
# platform (ADR-009: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04, linux/amd64). Path-filtered to
# the files that can break it.
?docker-build

# e2e.yml — the browser lane (VZ-FOUND-008). It builds the production image
# from this Dockerfile, runs it, and drives it with Playwright at 1440 px and
# 390 px, failing on any console error, uncaught exception, failed request or
# HTTP >= 400 response that is not allow-listed with a written reason. It is
# how the meta AGENTS.md's "exercise the running production-mode UI" stops
# being a sentence and starts being a gate, and every later UI slice proves
# itself through it.
#
# NOT path-filtered, on purpose: a required lane with a path filter passes by
# never running. Never demote it to `?e2e`.
e2e

# DELIBERATELY ABSENT: supply-chain.yml's `deps-scan` and `image-scan`.
#
# They run on every pull request and in the merge queue, fail loudly on HIGH or
# CRITICAL, and publish their reports as artifacts — they are simply not part
# of the required set yet, and the reason is not laziness. A scan lane's result
# depends on the world: a CVE published tomorrow against an unfixed package
# turns it red with no change to this repository. `ci-guard` forbids
# `continue-on-error`, correctly, so the only honest options are "required and
# occasionally red for reasons outside the PR" or "not required and read by a
# human". Until there is an agreed route for an unfixed upstream CVE — a
# reviewed, expiring .trivyignore.yaml entry — the second is the honest one. A
# required lane that goes red on its own is how a team learns to merge past red.
#
# Promoting them is an owner-reviewed change to THIS file and to the floor in
# scripts/ci/check-required-floor.sh. The baseline as of 2026-09-20 is zero
# findings in both lanes (see docs/evidence/), so the remaining condition is
# the CVE-handling route, not the baseline.
